Francisco Gold Condominium II Bldg, EDSA corner Mapagmahal St., Diliman, Quezon City OFFICE OF THE UNDERSECRETARY FOR LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG OPINION NO. 3 S. 2010 11 January 2010 MR. ALFONSO ZIJL Executive Director Bataris Formation Center Barangay Buhangin 3200 Baler Aurora Province Dear Mr. Van Zijt This has reference to your earlier letter seeking this Department's legal opinion on the following issues, which we quoted hereunder: "1) Is ir correct that the PDC shall only meet once a ear or at least twice a year:" 2) Is •orrect that this particular case (11 1'egular members) one iburth of fully organized council is S or -I, representatives of NGOs/Pos? S) Is ir correct that the regular members o/ • the council elect (b] secret voting) the (3) representatives of the NGOs/ POs from among the 6 accredited NGOs/ POs to rhe PDC, or the representarive.s oi all the accredited .AGOs/Pos elect amono• themselves would become members of' PDC?" In reply tc Dur first query, may we invite your attention to Section 110 of the Local Govern:nent Code of 1991 (RA 71 60), which provides that: "SECTION 110. Meetings and Quorum. —The local development council shall meet at least once every six (6) months or as often as may be necessary. " It is clear the aforequoted provision that local development councils (CDCs), in your case the provincial development council (PDC), is mandated by law to meet at least once every six (6) months or as often as may be necessary, meaning the PDC shall hold meetings at least twice a year. With regau--i to your second query, may we again invite your attention to Section 107 (c) oi the Local Government Code of 1991, thus: "SECTION 107. Composi tion of Local Development Councils . xxx xxx xxx

(c) The provincial development council shall be headed by the governor and shall be composed of the following members: (I) All mayors of component cities and municipalities; (2) The chairman of the committee on appropriations of the sangguniang panlalawigan; (3) The congressman or his representative; and (4) Representatives of nongovernmental organizations operating the province, who shall constitute not less than one-fourth (1/4) of the members the fully organized council. " (Emphasis Supplied) Based on the aforequoted provision of the Code, representatives of NGOs operating in the province shall constitute not less than 1/4 of the members of the fully organized council. Applying this to your case, if the fully organized council in your province is composed of eleven (11) regular members as represented in your letter, then of 11 is 2.75. But since there is no such thing as a fraction vote, the quotient of 2.75 shall now be rounded off to 3 which is the next whole number taking into account the ruling of the Supreme Court in the case of Santiago, et al. vs. Guingona, et al. (G.R. No. 134577, 18 November 1998). It is worth to emphasize that 2.75 should be round off to 3 because the law says "not less than one-fourth (1/4) xxx. Anent your third query, may we finally invite your attention to Section 108 of the Local Government Code of 1991 and Article 64 (d) of its Implementing Rules and Regulations (IRR), viz. "SECTION 108. Represen tat ion of Nongovernmental Organizations . —Within a period of sixty (60) days from the start of organization of local development councils, the nongovernmental organizations shall choose from among themselves their representatives to said councils. The local sanggunian concerned shall accredit nongovernmental organizations subject to such criteria as may be provided by law. " "ART. 64. Procedure and Guidelines for Selection of Represen ta tives of People' s Organizations , Nongovernmental Organizations or the Private Sector in LOC*I Special Bodies.—xxx xxx xxx (d) Meeting to choose representatives of people's organizations, NGOs, or the private sector — Within fifteen (15) days after the accreditation process, the DILG field officer assigned in the LGU shall call all accredited people's organizations, NGOs, or the private sector to a meeting where these organizations shall choose from among themselves which people's organizations, NGOs or private sector will be represented in the local special bodies. The selected people's organizations, NGOs or private sector shall then designate their principal and alternate representatives who are residents of the LGU concerned. In no case shall an organization or a representative thereof

be a member of more than one local special body within a province, city or municipality." Based on the aforequoted provision of the Code and its IRR, all the accredited NGOs, acting through their respective representatives, shall choose from among themselves in a meeting called for such purpose which organization shall be represented in the local special bodies. We hope that we have addressed your concern accordingly. Very truly yours, AUSTERE A. PANADER Undersecretar LY20:17/rnd cc: The Regional Director DILG Region Brgy.
